title: Local homology square for pullback of a bottom chain representative
statement: Let S and Y be schemes [def-pc-scheme], k:Y -> S, and f:X -> Z an arrow in D(O_S) [def-pc-derived-category]. Let U be an open of S and let A,B be strictly perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-complex] on its localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Suppose A^i=0 for i != 0, B^i=0 for i < 0, B.d(0,1)=0, and alpha:A -> B has invertible component alpha^0. Fix isomorphisms eA:X|U -> Q(A) and eB:Z|U -> Q(B) for which f|U >> eB = eA >> Q(alpha). For every y of Y with k(y) in U there is an open V containing y, complexes P,Q on the localized site over V, and beta:P -> Q, such that P^-1=Q^-1=0, P.d(0,1)=Q.d(0,1)=0 and beta^0 is invertible. There are isomorphisms eP:H0(Lk*X)|V -> H0(P) and eQ:H0(Lk*Z)|V -> H0(Q) such that H0(Lk*f)|V >> eQ = eP >> H0(beta), where derived pullback is [def-pc-derived-pullback]. No universal rank hypothesis or construction of the original model is asserted.

proof.text: Put V = k inverse-image U and construct F = Modules.localizedPullback k U, P = F(A), Q = F(B), beta = F(alpha) termwise. Use the standard derived category on the localized target site; its localization universe need not equal the ambient universe. Additivity maps the zero negative terms and zero outgoing differentials to zero, and F maps the invertible component alpha.f 0 to an invertible component.

Use the single natural transformation of lem-pc-localized-pullback-perfect-counit for both A and B. Its components there are invertible. Combine the universe-aware open-restriction natural isomorphism with the exact-functor composition isomorphisms. Map the supplied model square through the restricted derived pullback and compose the three squares: restriction naturality, the image of the given model square, and the counit naturality square for alpha. Reflect the result through the fully faithful derived open-site equivalence to obtain a square in the localized derived category.

Apply zeroth homology to this square. Compose it with the natural exact-restriction/homology isomorphism and the natural homology factorization through DerivedCategory.Q. The elementary compose_squares helper combines these three squares, yielding eP, eQ and exactly the requested equation for the specified morphism. V contains y by hy; no nonempty-open or positive-rank assumption is needed.

theorem bottom_chain_model_pullback_transport
    [∀ T : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace))]
    (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ U : S.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (X Z : schemeDerivedCategory S) (f : X ⟶ Z) (U : S.Opens)
    (A B : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hA : IsStrictlyPerfect S U A) (hB : IsStrictlyPerfect S U B)
    (hAzero : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → IsZero (A.X i))
    (hBnegative : ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero (B.X i))
    (hBzero : B.d 0 1 = 0) (α : A ⟶ B) (hα : IsIso (α.f 0))
    (eA : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj X ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj A)
    (eB : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj Z ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj B)
    (hsquare : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.map f ≫ eB.hom =
          eA.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map α)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (k : Y ⟶ S) (y : Y) (hy : k.base y ∈ U) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, y ∈ V ∧
      ∃ P Q : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over V)) ℤ,
        IsZero (P.X (-1)) ∧ IsZero (Q.X (-1)) ∧
        P.d 0 1 = 0 ∧ Q.d 0 1 = 0 ∧
        ∃ β : P ⟶ Q, IsIso (β.f 0) ∧
          ∃ (eP : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
              ((derivedPullback k).obj X)).over V ≅ P.homology 0)
            (eQ : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
              ((derivedPullback k).obj Z)).over V ≅ Q.homology 0),
            (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).map
                ((derivedPullback k).map f)).over V) ≫ eQ.hom =
                  eP.hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap β 0
